alt: Paper 1 is a 2-hour written exam worth 80 marks and 33.3% of the A-level. Education carries 50 marks, Methods in Context 20 marks and Theory and Methods 10 marks.
caption: Methods in Context is a 20-mark extended-writing question within Paper 1.

alt: Research methods knowledge from 3.1.3 Theory and Methods and substantive knowledge from 3.1.1 Education feed into 3.1.2 Methods in Context, which applies the first to the second.
caption: Methods in Context combines two other content areas instead of adding new content.

alt: Two overlapping circles: a feature of the method and a feature of the education context. Method-only and context-only answers score low; the overlap, explaining how the two interact, earns top-band marks.
caption: Marks come from linking a method feature to a feature of the education setting.

alt: Four education-specific issues to prepare: gatekeeper access through head teachers and parents, school timetabling constraints, the power imbalance between adult researchers and pupils, and informed consent with minors.
caption: Four practical and ethical issues that recur in school-based research.

after: ## Worked example: applying a method to an education research topic
alt: Three answers about using structured interviews to study teachers’ expectations of pupils: a method-only point and a context-only point both score low, while a combined point linking quick, standardised interviews to teachers’ time and the sensitivity of the topic scores high.
caption: The combined point links the method’s features to the features of this topic.

alt: Four steps: read the item for specific details, build points that combine a method feature with a context feature, develop three or four in depth while returning to the item, and finish with an overall judgement on whether the method suits the topic.
caption: Fewer, deeper combined points, ending with a judgement.
